$comment: THE ANTI-TELL VOCABULARY — one list, read by every surface that ships prose.
Extracted from apps/web/src/__tests__/aiVoiceGuard.test.ts on 2026-09-03, when a
second reader appeared. The guard scans SOURCE STRINGS: UI copy and Stormy's
system prompt. Draft Kit blurbs are database rows written through
data-pipeline/draftkit/load_blurbs.py, so they walked straight past it — the one
body of prose in the product that is sold rather than shipped had no voice rule
on it at all.
A Python copy of this list would drift from the TypeScript one inside a month.
This is the same problem scoringDefaults.json solves, and the same answer, with
one simplification: every pattern below uses only syntax that means the same
thing in JS and Python (\b, \s, \w, \d, (?:...), bounded {n,m}), so both
languages compile these strings directly and no generation step is needed.
Keep it that way — no lookbehind, no named groups, no \p{...}.
Patterns are matched case-insensitively by both readers.

bannedPhrases.name: it's not just X, it's Y

moatOverstatement.name: overstates pass-context coverage
moatOverstatement.$comment: The pass-context features cover 10,047 of the 118,975 shots scored in 2025, about 8%. Any sentence pairing them with every/all shots is false.

emDash.$comment: U+2014. Commas, periods and parentheses all exist. This is the single loudest tell and it is banned outright in anything a reader sees.

$comment: THE COPY-VOICE BANS (docs/COPY_VOICE.md, banned vocabulary; docs/DESIGN_DIRECTION.md rule 7).
Added 2026-09-03 as its own key, read by apps/web/src/__tests__/copyVoiceGuard.test.ts.
aiVoiceGuard reads bannedPhrases, accuracyClaims, moatOverstatement and emDash only,
so nothing here changes what that guard scans or how it reports.
toastTitles   match a whole `title:` literal. The count of `title: "Error"` in the app
reached 0 on 2026-09-03; these are what stop the 56th.
phrases       are tested against EVERY string literal and JSX text run a person could
read (comparison operands and logger arguments excluded).
rawErrorCodes are tested against sentence-shaped literals only: 'ERR_NETWORK' as a
code constant is data, and only becomes a defect once it sits in prose.
budgets       are the brevity budgets, in the units COPY_VOICE states them in. The guard
pins them to the numbers in the doc, so change the doc first.
Same portability rule as the rest of this file: no lookbehind, no named groups,
no \p{...}. Matched case-insensitively.

rawErrorCodes.name: a Node or Chromium network code
an HTTP status number
rawErrorCodes.pattern: \b(?:http|status(?:\s+code)?|error(?:\s+code)?)\s*[:#]?\s*[45]\d\d\b|\b[45]\d\d\s+(?:internal server error|bad gateway|service unavailable|gateway time-?out|not found|forbidden|unauthorized|bad request)\b

rawErrorCodes.name: a JavaScript runtime fault
rawErrorCodes.pattern: \[object object\]|\b(?:type|reference|syntax|range)error\b|\bundefined is not\b|\bcannot read propert|\bis not a function\b|\bis not defined\b
